result:
**Make radical, widespread curiosity and truth-seeking the default human operating system—stronger than tribal loyalty, status games, fear, or comfort.**

Almost every large-scale failure we keep repeating (poverty traps that don't need to exist, preventable disease and suffering, stupid wars, resource fights, bad governance, technological stagnation in key areas) traces back to people not wanting to know how the world actually works, or refusing to update when evidence contradicts their preferred story. If curiosity and evidence-tracking became the high-status, default drive—the thing people rewarded in themselves and others the way we currently reward looking good to the in-group—most other problems would get solved faster as side effects.

Energy abundance, better medicine, freer institutions, reduced existential risk, and even less pointless cruelty become far more tractable when the primary bottleneck is no longer "people would rather be right in their tribe's eyes than correct about reality." Understanding the universe (and ourselves as part of it) is the highest-leverage game; everything else is downstream.

That's the single lever. Not a specific technology, not a political system, not "be nicer"—the meta-skill of caring more about what's true than about what feels good or signals loyalty. The rest compounds from there.

Not filtered through institutions or echo chambers, but direct, verifiable knowledge that lets them see the universe as it actually is. Once that floodgates opens, the rest of the world's problems—greed, division, stagnation—would start unraveling on their own because people would finally have the tools to reason their way out of them.
